prf:t-beta-markov-frobenius-collapse:
Proof Proof of t beta markov frobenius collapse. Completing the square.

Let X \in H satisfy the constraint \mathrm{tr}_M(X) = S. Write the decomposition X = (X - S \cdot 1) + S \cdot 1 and expand the Frobenius norm-squared:

\| X \|^2_\tau = \mathrm{tr}_M(X X^\dagger)
              = \mathrm{tr}_M\big((X - S \cdot 1)(X - S \cdot 1)^\dagger\big)
                + S \, \mathrm{tr}_M(X + X^\dagger) - S^2 \, \mathrm{tr}_M(1).

(The scalar S \cdot 1 is central and fixed by \dagger, so (X - S \cdot 1)(X - S \cdot 1)^\dagger = X X^\dagger - S(X + X^\dagger) + S^2 \cdot 1. Since \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w) = \mathrm{tr}_M(T_{w^{-1}}), the trace is \dagger-invariant, so \mathrm{tr}_M(X^\dagger) = \mathrm{tr}_M(X) = S; applying linearity term by term gives the identity above.)

Substituting the Markov normalisation \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1 and the constraint \mathrm{tr}_M(X) = S:

\| X \|^2_\tau = \| X - S \cdot 1 \|^2_\tau + 2 S^2 - S^2
             = \| X - S \cdot 1 \|^2_\tau + S^2.

The twisted form is positive-semi-definite: in the orthogonal seminormal form each \sigma_i is real symmetric, so \dagger is the blockwise transpose and \| Y \|^2_\tau = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \, \| Y_\lambda \|_F^2 \ge 0, since every Markov weight y_\lambda \ge 0. Therefore

\| X \|^2_\tau \;\ge\; S^2,

with equality iff \| X - S \cdot 1 \|^2_\tau = 0, i.e. iff X - S \cdot 1 vanishes on every block with y_\lambda > 0. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the blocks with y_\lambda = 0 are exactly the shapes with three or more rows, so the minimiser is S \cdot 1 up to that radical. (The untwisted form \mathrm{tr}_M(X \cdot X) cannot be used: it is negative on \sigma_1\sigma_2 - \sigma_2\sigma_1 \in H_3.)

Therefore T_\beta = S \cdot 1 is a minimum-Frobenius-norm primal-feasible element, with \| T_\beta \|^2_\tau = S^2. \quad\blacksquare
prop:t-beta-markov-frobenius-collapse-ge:
Proposition Min-Frobenius-norm collapse: T_β = S · 1_A — general unital R-algebra lift of [prop:t-beta-markov-frobenius-collapse]. Let R be a strict-ordered field. Let A be a unital R-algebra. Let \tau : A \to R be an R-linear normalised trace (\tau(1) = 1, \tau(xy) = \tau(yx)). Let X \mapsto X^\dagger be an R-linear anti-multiplicative map on A ((XY)^\dagger = Y^\dagger X^\dagger) with 1^\dagger = 1 and \tau(X^\dagger) = \tau(X). Assume the twisted form is positive-semi-definite: 0 \le \tau(Y \cdot Y^\dagger) for all Y \in A. For any S \in R and X \in A satisfying \tau(X) = S:

S^2 \;\le\; \tau(X \cdot X^\dagger).

If the twisted form is non-degenerate (\tau(Y \cdot Y^\dagger) = 0 \implies Y = 0), the lower bound is attained if and only if X = S \cdot 1_A.

When A is commutative, taking X^\dagger = X recovers the untwisted statement S^2 \le \tau(X \cdot X) under positivity of \tau on squares.

prop:binding-genfun-qdifference:
Proposition The binding generating function's q-difference equation gives a depth-d recurrence. Let G(x;q)=\sum_{n\geq 0} B_n(K)\,x^n be the generating function of the body-order binding terms (Binding many-body series equals the jet-order filtration: B(K)=\sum_n m_e\,a_D^{(n)}). Suppose G satisfies a fibre-level q-difference equation

G(qx;q) \;=\; R(q,x)\,G(x;q),
\qquad R(q,x)\in\mathbb{Q}(q)[x,x^{-1}]\ \text{of bounded depth }d .

Then:

  1. Linear q-recurrence. Writing R = \sum_j r_j(q)\,x^j, the body terms satisfy an order-d linear recurrence whose coefficients depend on the position through q^n; for polynomial R, (q^n - r_0)\,B_n = \sum_{j=1}^{d} r_j\,B_{n-j}. Every term is fixed by R and the first d terms, so whatever growth the B_n show is an output of R, not a fitted constant. The coefficients are not constant in n: for R = 1 - x the solution B_n = 1/(q;q)_n gives 1, -1, 1/3, -1/21, 1/315 at q = 2, which satisfies no constant-coefficient recurrence of depth 1 or 2.
  2. Archimedean image. Under the realisation functor \tau at q=q_0, the q-difference equation passes to a linear (Dirac-type) differential equation on the realised generating function: the fibre q-shift becomes a derivation in the archimedean limit.

The implications (1)--(2) are the standard passage from a q-holonomic generating function to a q-recursive coefficient sequence (coefficients polynomial in q^n) and its confluent (differential) limit; they hold for any such R. What is open is the existence and identity of the kernel R for the binding G. By the precision-floor obstruction — the c_k information bound, which makes term data unmeasurable beyond low order — R cannot be fixed by fitting the B_n; it must be derived from the fibre root-of-unity singularity structure of the Seiberg--Witten differential (The Seiberg–Witten period is an algebraic residue sum). This is the same q-difference machinery as the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta precision ladder, applied to the binding series.

Scope of the rank-1 hypothesis — unsatisfiable on both proposed carriers; the proposition survives only in rank 2. The supposition above is a first-order (rank-1) q-difference relation. Two carriers have been proposed for G, and neither admits one.

The raw carrier — the ordinary generating function of the raw body terms B_n = I(n)/n — was excluded by the confluent/Gevrey growth argument (proved). That exclusion explicitly re-targeted the conjecture at the q-Borel / Gevrey-normalized carrier b_n = f_n/[n]_q!, predicting depth d = 2. The normalized carrier provably satisfies [m+2]_q\,b_{m+2} = b_{m+1} + b_m, i.e. the operator L_{\mathcal{K}} = (q^2x-1)\sigma^2 - (q-1)\sigma - (q-1).

A scalar kernel is a first-order right factor \sigma - a of L_{\mathcal{K}}, i.e. a solution a\in K(x) of the q-Riccati equation (q^2x-1)\,a(qx)\,a(x) - (q-1)\,a(x) - (q-1) = 0. Writing a = P/Q and clearing denominators, the three terms have degrees 1+2p, p+u and 2u with p = \deg P, u = \deg Q. The first is odd-shaped and the third even, so 1+2p = 2u is impossible over \mathbb{Z}; a two-line case split then gives that the maximum is attained exactly once for every (p,u), and a lone top-degree term cannot cancel. Hence no rational a exists, \mathcal{K} is irreducible of rank 2, and no nonzero solution of L_{\mathcal{K}} obeys any scalar relation G(qx) = R(q,x)G(x) with R \in K(x) — a fortiori none with R\in\mathbb{Q}(q)[x,x^{-1}] of any depth d; the depth never enters the argument, only the degrees do. This exclusion is proved.

Scope (b), structural exclusion, invariant cited. The parity is the Newton-slope invariant: L_{\mathcal{K}} is pure isoclinic of slope \tfrac12 at infinity, every rank-1 q-difference module has integer slope, and Newton slopes are additive on sub- and quotient modules. Independently corroborated by the van der Put--Reversat classification of pure modules [vanderput-reversat2007, vanderput2006]: a pure module of non-integral slope d/r, \gcd(d,r)=1, and rank r is E(r,d,b) in Bugeaud's notation [bugeaud2011], and it is irreducible.

What survives. Implications (1)--(2) are unaffected and the depth-2 prediction stands — but depth 2 means rank 2: the kernel is a 2\times2 matrix A(q,x) acting on (G, \sigma G), whose \tau-image is a first-order two-component system, which is what "Dirac-type" already asks for. Restated in rank 2 the proposition is intact; restated in rank 1 it is vacuous. The exclusion is over K(x): after a degree-2 ramified base change (adjoining q^{1/2}, x^{1/2}) the slope becomes the integer 1 and a scalar kernel does exist on the double cover, relating half-shifts — that is, even and odd body orders separately. That ramification is the missing structure, not a gap in the argument.

Geometric target of the kernel module (literature). Fix q\in\mathbb{C} with 0<|q|<1 and let K=\mathbb{C}(\{z\}) be the field of germs of meromorphic functions at 0, with \varphi(z)=qz. Van der Put and Reversat show that a q-difference module M over K induces functorially a vector bundle v(M) on the Tate curve \mathbb{C}^{*}/q^{\mathbb{Z}}, for all slopes, and recover Atiyah's classification of indecomposable bundles on that curve as a corollary [vanderput-reversat2007, Introduction, §2]. Two points of convention apply before this is used here. First, the kernel module \mathcal{K} above is stated over K(x) with q an indeterminate and its slope is read at x=\infty, so the functor applies only after q is specialised to a complex number with |q|\neq 1 and the module is passed to germs at a point; for |q|>1, as at the substrate value q_0, one replaces (q,\Phi) by (q^{-1},\Phi^{-1}), which leaves the lattice q^{\mathbb{Z}}, and so the curve, unchanged. Second, the Tate curve \mathbb{C}^{*}/q^{\mathbb{Z}} is not the Descartes elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_q of the Descartes elliptic curve; the symbol \mathcal{E}_q keeps that meaning, and the bundle v(\mathcal{K}) itself is not constructed in this paper.
prf:binding-genfun-qdifference:
Proof Proof of the q-difference recurrence of the binding generating function. Write G(x;q)=\sum_{n\geq 0}B_n x^n and, for polynomial R, R(q,x)=\sum_{j=0}^{d} r_j(q)\,x^{j}. The coefficient of x^{n} in G(qx;q) is q^{n}B_{n}, and in R(q,x)G(x;q) it is \sum_{j=0}^{d} r_j B_{n-j}. Hence

  (q^{n} - r_0)\,B_{n} \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{d} r_j\,B_{n-j},

and for q^n \neq r_0 this solves for B_n in terms of B_{n-1},\dots,B_{n-d} with coefficients r_j/(q^n - r_0), rational in q and q^n. A Laurent R shifts the indices but leaves the factor q^n on the B_n coefficient. This is the standard fact that a q-holonomic series has q-recursive coefficients; it fixes every term from R and the first d terms. (Note that the factor q^n makes the recurrence coefficients r_j/(q^n - r_0) depend explicitly on the index n, rather than being constant in n.)

For the Archimedean image, apply \tau at q=q_0 and let q\to q_0 act on the shift operator x\mapsto qx: the multiplicative q-shift degenerates to the infinitesimal generator x\,\partial_x (the confluent limit of a q-difference operator), so G(qx;q)=R(q,x)G(x;q) passes to a linear differential equation x\,\partial_x \widehat{G} = \rho(x)\,\widehat{G} on the realised \widehat{G}=\tau G — the Dirac-type equation. Given the depth-d recurrence, with position-dependent coefficients, the term identity follows; the existence of R for the binding G is the conjectural input (carried as a hypothesis). \qquad\blacksquare

The alignment. The cyclotomic-pure regime n \leq 5 coincides exactly with the framework's calibration orders and the quintic order:

\{\,n \leq 5 : D(n)\text{ cyclotomic}\,\}
\;=\;
\underbrace{\{n=2,3,4\}}_{\text{calibration orders } c=1,2,3}
\;\cup\;
\underbrace{\{n=5\}}_{S_5\text{ quintic order}}.

The first non-cyclotomic (non-q-holonomic) content appears at the first body order n=6 that is neither a calibration nor the quintic order.

The arithmetic mechanism. At q=1 one has S(n)|_{q=1} = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} f^\lambda = I(n), the involution / telephone numbers (OEIS A000085; the Frobenius–Schur identity, proved for all n by RSK: involutions \leftrightarrow SYT). So S(n) is the q-deformed involution number — a Rogers–Szegő / q-Hermite moment — and the recurrence above is the q-lift of I(n)=I(n-1)+(n-1)I(n-2), with D(n) its deviation. Why the individual quantum dimensions do not locate the boundary. Every \dim_q(\lambda) = [n]_q!/\prod_c [h(c)]_q is a product of cyclotomic polynomials for every n (a ratio of cyclotomic products that is a polynomial). So cyclotomic-purity of the individual dimensions does not distinguish n=5 from n=6: at both orders all \dim_q(\lambda) are cyclotomic. In particular the McKay observation below — that at n=5 the four classes carry single quantum integers while at n=6 most are compound products of several [m]_q — is a single-[m]_q-vs-product distinction, not a cyclotomic-vs-non-cyclotomic one (a product of several cyclotomics is still cyclotomic). It does not, by itself, supply the arithmetic mechanism above.

The McKay coincidence (rep-theory, link unproven). At the quintic order n=5 the four conjugation classes \{\lambda,\lambda'\} of S_5 carry quantum dimensions equal to the E_8 Coxeter marks [\mathrm{mark}]_q:

\dim_q(5)=[1]_q,\quad
\dim_q(4,1)=[4]_q,\quad
\dim_q(3,2)=[5]_q,\quad
\dim_q(3,1,1)=[5]_q+1,

because A_5 \cong 2I/\{\pm 1\} is the icosahedral group and 2I \leftrightarrow \widehat{E}_8 (McKay). The McKay–ADE ladder of alternating groups is finite: A_4 \cong tetrahedral (2T \leftrightarrow \widehat{E}_6), A_5 \cong icosahedral (2I \leftrightarrow \widehat{E}_8), and A_6 \cong \mathrm{PSL}(2,9) is not a binary polyhedral group. That the McKay-mark structure exits at the same order the tail leaves the cyclotomic ring is a coincidence of orders; by the caveat above it does not act through cyclotomic-purity of the dimensions, and its bearing on the arithmetic mechanism is unproven.

Status — three tiers of correlation, not to be conflated.

  1. Arithmetic (the substance): D(n) is non-cyclotomic from n=6. This is verified through n=11 but not proved for all n \geq 6; the cofactor's non-q-holonomic degree growth is the structural reason, not yet a proof. Generic high-degree bar-even integer polynomials are non-cyclotomic, so non-cyclotomicity is the expected outcome — the content is entirely that n \leq 5 are cyclotomic, and that "for all n \geq 6, with no exceptions" is what a proof must supply.

prop:jet-filtration-binding-extensive:
Proposition The jet-filtration binding is extensive (monotone in body order). Stated over \mathbb{R} (archimedean regime); the combinatorial content is a finite non-negative sum.

The body-order series supplies it, because each term \mathfrak{m}_e a_D^{(n)} w_n is a non-negative contribution and the number of terms grows with A.

prop:tower-geometric-lower-bound:

  \tfrac{1}{30}\,\bigl(\sqrt{2}\bigr)^{k} \;\leq\; w_{\mathrm{std}}(k) \qquad (k \geq 3).

Below k = 3 the weight is exactly zero, not small: no Young diagram of fewer than three cells contains (2,1), and the skew count f^{\lambda/\mu} is defined to vanish off containment. So k \geq 3 is the whole range on which any positive lower bound is possible, and a bound asserted for every k is false rather than open.

The geometric form is a weaker shadow of what is proved. The underlying result is the square bound k!/(81 \cdot 2^{k}) \leq w_{\mathrm{std}}(k)^{2}, valid for k \geq 3, which is genuinely super-exponential since k!/2^{k} outgrows every geometric sequence. prop:level-selection-not-linear:
Proposition Linear level-selection is excluded (exponential beats linear). Let w = w_{\mathrm{std}} be the branched brane-tower weight, which by Brane-tower growth above the containment threshold (GAP-A-3) satisfies c\,r^{k} \leq w(k) for k \geq 3 with r = \sqrt{2} > 1 and c = 1/30 > 0. If the binding is extensive — w(A) \leq M \cdot A for every A \geq 1 — then a contradiction follows. Consequently no linear level-selection rule k(A) = A (nor bond-count k(A) = A(A-1)/2, a fortiori) is consistent with extensive binding: the selected jet level grows at most logarithmically in A.

Proof idea. The tower bound gives c\,r^{A} \leq w(A) \leq M\cdot A for all A \geq 1. But a geometric c\,r^{A} with r > 1 eventually outgrows any linear M\cdot A — formally (A) = o(r^{A}) as A \to \infty — so the inequality cannot hold for all A. Dividing the surviving bound by c and taking \log_r shows k(A) \leq \log_r\!\big((M/c)\,A\big), i.e. at most logarithmic growth.

Restriction of the hypothesis to A \geq 1. Extensivity is imposed only for A \geq 1, the physical regime. Excluding A = 0 ensures the exclusion is the genuine growth argument rather than a degenerate boundary coincidence: at A = 0 the linear side is M \cdot 0 = 0, so the inequality would fail or hold for reasons unrelated to the exponential-versus-linear mechanism.

The tower bound does not force w(0) \geq c > 0: w_{\mathrm{std}}(0) = 0, because no diagram of fewer than three cells contains (2,1). Stated for every k, the growth hypothesis would be false at k = 0, so the A = 0 case is a falsity in the antecedent rather than a boundary effect in the conclusion. That is why Brane-tower growth above the containment threshold (GAP-A-3) now carries a threshold, and why this proposition is unconditional rather than conditional.

\bar\mu_{ijk} \equiv m_{ijk}(F) - t_{ijk}(F) \pmod{\delta},

It is not shown here to be a binding channel: whether \Psi_{ijk} is well defined on the corpus's braid words under its closure and basepoint conventions, and whether it has the right scale for a binding term, are both unchecked.

prop:binding-period-involution-statistic:
Proposition The balanced dimension sum is the involution generating function for 2\,\mathrm{maj} + \mathrm{content} \circ \mathrm{RSK}. For n \geq 1 let [k] = (q^k - q^{-k})/(q - q^{-1}) denote the balanced quantum integer, and for a partition \lambda \vdash n with hook lengths h(c), c \in \lambda, set

\dim_q^{\mathrm{bal}}(\lambda) \;=\; \frac{\prod_{k=1}^{n} [k]}{\prod_{c \in \lambda} [h(c)]},
\qquad
S^{\mathrm{bal}}(n; q) \;=\; \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \dim_q^{\mathrm{bal}}(\lambda).

For an involution w \in \mathrm{Inv}(S_n) let \lambda(w) be its RSK shape, let \mathrm{maj}(w) = \sum_{i \in \mathrm{Des}(w)} i be its major index, where \mathrm{Des}(w) = \{\, i : w(i) > w(i+1) \,\} is the descent set, and let \mathrm{content}(\lambda) = \sum_{(i,j) \in \lambda} (j - i) be the content sum of a shape. Then

S^{\mathrm{bal}}(n; q)\, q^{n(n-1)/2}
\;=\;
\sum_{w \in \mathrm{Inv}(S_n)} q^{\,2\,\mathrm{maj}(w) + \mathrm{content}(\lambda(w))} .

In particular both sides specialise at q = 1 to the involution count I(n). The common value is a polynomial in q of degree

\deg \;=\; n^{2} \;-\; H_{\min}(n),
\qquad
H_{\min}(n) \;=\; \min_{\lambda \vdash n} \sum_{c \in \lambda} h(c),

the minimum being over partitions of n of the total hook length. Writing T_k = k(k+1)/2, this minimum is itself closed-form,

H_{\min}(n) \;=\; 2n - 1 \;+\; \sum_{k \ge 2,\; T_k \le n-1} (n - T_k)
\;=\; \tfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}\, n^{3/2} + O(n),

attained at the staircase (k, k-1, \dots, 1) when n = T_k is triangular, where it equals the square pyramidal number k(k+1)(2k+1)/6.
prf:binding-period-involution-statistic:
Proof Proof that the balanced dimension sum is the 2\,\mathrm{maj} + \mathrm{content} \circ \mathrm{RSK} involution generating function. Write b(\lambda) = \sum_{i \geq 1} (i-1)\lambda_i, so that \mathrm{content}(\lambda) = b(\lambda') - b(\lambda) with \lambda' the conjugate partition, and let [k]_q = 1 + q + \cdots + q^{k-1} denote the unbalanced quantum integer and \tilde f^{\lambda}(q) = q^{b(\lambda)} [n]_q! / \prod_{c \in \lambda} [h(c)]_q the fake degree of \lambda \vdash n [stanley1999].

Step 1 (balanced twist). From [k] = (q^k - q^{-k})/(q - q^{-1}) = q^{-(k-1)}[k]_{q^2} and the hook-length identity \sum_{c \in \lambda} h(c) = b(\lambda) + b(\lambda') + n,

\dim_q^{\mathrm{bal}}(\lambda)
= q^{\sum_{c}(h(c)-1) \, - \, \sum_{k=1}^{n}(k-1)}
  \cdot \frac{\prod_{k=1}^{n}[k]_{q^2}}{\prod_{c \in \lambda}[h(c)]_{q^2}}
= q^{\,\mathrm{content}(\lambda) - n(n-1)/2}\; \tilde f^{\lambda}(q^2).

Step 2 (q-hook-maj). Stanley's formula gives, for every \lambda \vdash n, \sum_{T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda)} q^{\mathrm{maj}(T)} = \tilde f^{\lambda}(q) [stanley1999].

Step 3 (descent preservation on involutions). RSK restricts to a bijection w \mapsto P(w) from the involutions of RSK shape \lambda onto \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda), and \mathrm{Des}(w) = \mathrm{Des}(P(w)) (Schützenberger) [sagan2001]; hence \mathrm{maj}(w) = \mathrm{maj}(P(w)) and

\sum_{w \in \mathrm{Inv}(S_n),\; \lambda(w) = \lambda} q^{\,2\,\mathrm{maj}(w)}
= \tilde f^{\lambda}(q^2).

Multiplying by q^{\mathrm{content}(\lambda)}, summing over \lambda \vdash n, and applying Step 1 termwise yields \sum_{w} q^{2\,\mathrm{maj}(w) + \mathrm{content}(\lambda(w))} = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} q^{\mathrm{content}(\lambda)} \tilde f^{\lambda}(q^2) = q^{n(n-1)/2} S^{\mathrm{bal}}(n; q). The q = 1 specialisation counts the standard Young tableaux, \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} f^{\lambda} = I(n) with f^{\lambda} = \tilde f^{\lambda}(1) their number per shape. \blacksquare

Verification. For n = 3, 4 the identity is also proved by deciding the exponent multisets from the computable RSK insertion; exact symbolic verification for n \leq 8 (all 764 involutions at n = 8) has been carried out, and the transfer-operator reconstruction extends the exact cross-checks to n \leq 16 (hook side) and n \leq 24 (at q = 1).

prop:content-genfun-palindromic:
Proposition The content generating function C_n(q) = \sum_\lambda f^\lambda q^{\mathrm{content}(\lambda)} is palindromic and bar-even. For n \geq 1 let f^\lambda be the number of standard Young tableaux of shape \lambda \vdash n and \mathrm{content}(\lambda) = \sum_{(i,j)\in\lambda}(j-i) the content sum, and set

C_n(q) \;=\; \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} f^\lambda\, q^{\,\mathrm{content}(\lambda)} .

Then C_n is palindromic,

C_n(q) \;=\; C_n(q^{-1}),

and its deviation from the classical value is bar-even of second order,

C_n(q) - C_n(1) \;=\; O\!\big((q-1)^2\big),
\qquad C_n(1) = \sum_{\lambda\vdash n} f^\lambda = I(n),

where I(n) is the number of involutions of S_n.

By balanced dimension sum as an involution generating function, C_n(q) is the content-only face of the binding statistic — the object obtained by retaining the RSK shape and discarding the descent (major-index) data. The bar-even O((q-1)^2) deviation is exactly the q-rigidity measured for the level-1/2 alien datum \Delta_{\omega_0}: the content sector carries no linear q-deformation, so it activates only at second order.

Both statements are instances of a single structural fact — partition conjugation \lambda \mapsto \lambda' is an anti-invariant involution, f^{\lambda'} = f^\lambda and \mathrm{content}(\lambda') = -\mathrm{content}(\lambda) — which is proved for every n; it gives the palindromy and the vanishing linear term \sum_\lambda f^\lambda\,\mathrm{content}(\lambda) = 0. The n=4 instance is proved directly: C_4(q) = q^6 + 3q^2 + 2 + 3q^{-2} + q^{-6}.
prf:content-genfun-palindromic:
Proof Proof that C_n(q) is palindromic and bar-even via the conjugation anti-involution. Partition conjugation \lambda \mapsto \lambda' is an involution of the set of partitions of n. It is weight-preserving, f^{\lambda'} = f^\lambda (the standard tableaux of \lambda' are the transposes of those of \lambda), and content-reversing, \mathrm{content}(\lambda') = -\mathrm{content}(\lambda) (transposition exchanges the row and column indices, negating each cell's content j-i).

Palindromy. Reindexing the sum by conjugation,

C_n(q^{-1}) = \sum_{\lambda} f^\lambda q^{-\mathrm{content}(\lambda)}
= \sum_{\lambda} f^{\lambda'} q^{-\mathrm{content}(\lambda')}
= \sum_{\lambda} f^{\lambda} q^{\,\mathrm{content}(\lambda)} = C_n(q),

using f^{\lambda'}=f^\lambda and -\mathrm{content}(\lambda') = \mathrm{content}(\lambda).

Bar-even second order. Writing q = e^t, the linear term of C_n(e^t) in t is \sum_\lambda f^\lambda\,\mathrm{content}(\lambda); the same reindexing gives \sum_\lambda f^\lambda\,\mathrm{content}(\lambda) = \sum_\lambda f^{\lambda'}\,\mathrm{content}(\lambda') = -\sum_\lambda f^\lambda\,\mathrm{content}(\lambda), hence it is 0. So C_n(q) - C_n(1) has no linear term and is O((q-1)^2). Finally C_n(1) = \sum_\lambda f^\lambda = I(n) is the classical identity counting involutions by RSK shape. \blacksquare

Verification. The two structural steps — reindexing by an anti-invariant involution for palindromy, and the vanishing first moment for bar-evenness — are proved for arbitrary finite index sets. The n=4 instance is checked concretely. Exact symbolic verification of the closed form, palindromy, C_n(1)=I(n) and the second-order rigidity has been carried out for n \leq 8, together with the parallel result for the Plancherel weight (f^\lambda)^2.
